instruction: Revise sentences containing forms of "is" (are, is, was, were, be, being, been) unless the form is necessary.
source_quote: Underline or highlight the forms of “is”—are, is, was, were, be, being, been—these sentences likely need revision

instruction: Find the action in each sentence and make it the verb.
source_quote: Find the action and make it the verb

instruction: Make the topic of the story the subject of the sentence.
source_quote: Make the topic of the story the subject

instruction: Determine what the subject does in the sentence and make that the verb.
source_quote: Determine what it does in the sentence and make that the verb

instruction: Replace wordy phrases with single words and complex words with simple ones.
source_quote: Replace wordy phrases with single words and complex words with simple ones

instruction: Use specific words.
source_quote: Use specific words

instruction: Avoid vague subjects such as nonspecific nouns like "studies" or pronouns.
source_quote: the subject is vague—either something nonspecific, like “studies,” or a pronoun—and the verb doesn’t tell us anything either

instruction: Remove words that don't add meaning, since they obscure the point of the sentence.
source_quote: Words that don’t add meaning obscure the point of the sentence

instruction: Keep the proportion of prepositions low so sentences don't read like a list.
source_quote: A high proportion of prepositions makes a sentence sound like a list

instruction: Identify the actor for the action in each sentence, if there is one.
source_quote: Identify the actor for that action, if there is one

instruction: Put the action of the sentence in the verb.
source_quote: 4) Put the action in the verb By “put the action in the verb,” I don’t necessarily mean that you must put the verb in the active voice—grammatical structure isn’t as important as using the verb to express something important.

instruction: Use a passive construction when the actor is unknown or unimportant.
source_quote: In cases where the actor is unknown or unimportant, you would need a passive construction.

instruction: Make the actor the subject so subjects match throughout the paragraph.
source_quote: Making the actor the subject makes subjects more similar throughout the paragraph—makes clear what the story’s about

instruction: Keep an “is” when the actor is irrelevant or it allows a logical order of information.
source_quote: an “is” can make a sentence or paragraph better: when the actor is irrelevant to the message and the overall story (as in the example and in methods sections2), and when this allows a logical order of information.

instruction: Eliminate only those “is”es that are unnecessary and get in the way of the message.
source_quote: the goal of this revision is to eliminate only those “is”es that are unnecessary and get in the way of the sentence’s message.

instruction: Place previously introduced information at the beginning of the sentence to provide context for new information.
source_quote: A logical order (see the lesson 12, “Revising sentence structure for coherence”) places information previously introduced at the beginning of the sentence so that it provides context for new information.

instruction: If identifying the action is difficult, find the term most closely related to the paragraph's topic and determine what it does in the sentence.
source_quote: consider looking for the term most closely related to the topic of the paragraph and determining what it does in the sentence. This will tell you what the verb would be to make clear what the action is.

instruction: Omit the actor when its identity is unknown or unimportant to the meaning.
source_quote: This often happens because the identity of the actor can’t be identified or isn’t important to the meaning of the sentence.

instruction: Delete words and phrases that add no meaning to the paragraph.
source_quote: Delete any words or phrases that don’t add meaning to the paragraph

instruction: Replace wordy phrases and complex words with shorter equivalents.
source_quote: Look for wordy phrases or unnecessarily complex words that mean the same thing as a single or shorter word, and replace them

instruction: Cut sentence parts that repeat or are implied by other parts.
source_quote: if any part of a sentence says the same thing as another part of that sentence or an adjacent sentence, or if any part says something implied by the rest, cut it.

instruction: Put the action in the verb and make clear who or what is doing it.
source_quote: making clear what’s happening (putting the action in the verb provides a structural clue to readers) and who or what is doing it in each sentence.

instruction: Use specific words that state exactly what you mean.
source_quote: Your words should tell the reader exactly what you mean—they should be specific.

instruction: State the direction of change or regulation instead of vague verbs.
source_quote: Rather than “regulate,” say “activate” or “inhibit;” rather than “alter,” “change,” or “adjust,” say “increase” or “decrease.”

instruction: Replace vague quantity words with actual numbers.
source_quote: If you see words like “some” or “several” or “many,” replace them with the number

instruction: Replace vague adverbs of degree with the proportion or percent of change.
source_quote: if you see change verbs modified with “greatly” or “somewhat,” replace the vague adverb with the proportion or percent of change.

instruction: Give each actor its own clause or sentence when a sentence has more than one actor.
source_quote: Such an overloaded sentence could be revised by separating each actor into its own clause or sentence, so that they each get their own verb.

instruction: Use the passive voice in methods sections.
source_quote: In methods sections, it makes more sense to use the passive voice than the active.

instruction: Be careful with vague words like systems, role, mechanism, factor, and process, and check they add meaning.
source_quote: Such words don’t have very specific meanings, and thus aren’t often useful. Others like it include “role,” “mechanism,” “factor,” and “process;” be careful when using such words.

instruction: Include in each figure all data supporting a single result so each results section explains one figure.
source_quote: each figure should contain all of the data that support a single result, so that each section of the results explains a single figure

instruction: Order figures to tell the most interesting logical story, not the chronological order of experiments.
source_quote: This order won’t necessarily be the order in which you performed the experiments; instead, it should be the order that tells the most interesting story possible

instruction: Place each figure immediately after the one whose result raises the question it addresses.
source_quote: imagine what question each figure or table would bring up and place the figure that addresses that question immediately after

instruction: Do not connect discontinuous data with lines.
source_quote: discontinuous data (where the values on the x axis are categories or where the distance between them does not reflect their numerical values) cannot be connected with lines

instruction: Indicate non-parametric data with medians rather than means.
source_quote: non-parametric data (where the values in a group do not follow a normal or Gaussian distribution) should be indicated by medians rather than means

instruction: Use a table when the values themselves matter.
source_quote: If the values themselves matter, use a table

instruction: Show only the aspect of the data that matters to your point.
source_quote: figures should only show as much as is necessary to make the point you intend and no more, as extraneous elements make identifying the point more difficult

instruction: Minimize non-data elements in each figure panel.
source_quote: show the data and minimize everything else

instruction: Include quantification when the magnitude of a difference matters.
source_quote: if the magnitude of the difference in fluorescence intensity or band density matters, you must include quantification

instruction: State the result in the figure legend title.
source_quote: Title states result

instruction: Keep figure legends to just enough information to interpret the figure.
source_quote: Just enough information to interpret figure

instruction: Represent data honestly in figures.
source_quote: Represent data honestly

instruction: Eliminate nonessential non-data elements such as gridlines and redundant labels to maximize the data-ink ratio.
source_quote: One way to maximize the data-ink ratio is to minimize the amount of non-data-ink by eliminating all nonessential elements, such as gridlines, and reducing the amount of ink used for other non-data elements as much as possible.

instruction: Show the change or comparison directly in the graph rather than making readers mentally calculate it.
source_quote: if the point of a graph is to show that a drug causes a greater decrease in uptake in one genotype than another, the graph should show the change directly so the reader doesn’t have to mentally calculate it.

instruction: Label elements of the graph directly to reduce shifting attention between graphics and legend.
source_quote: This can be avoided by labeling as much of the graph as possible, for example by using colored text in the upper corner of a fluorescence micrograph to indicate what each color represents.

instruction: Keep figures consistent with field conventions and with one another, including colors and axis ranges.
source_quote: Another way to make figure interpretation simpler is to keep figures consistent with the conventions of the field and with one another.

instruction: Use the same axis range for graphs that will be compared.
source_quote: if multiple graphs are to be compared, use the same range for all of those panels so that the sizes of bars or positions of points have the same relationship to their value.

instruction: Ensure distances in figures are proportional to the data values they represent.
source_quote: Distances should be proportional to values

instruction: Indicate axes that do not start at zero or use non-linear scales with a line break or appropriate tick marks.
source_quote: Such choices include starting an axis at a value other than zero without indicating it by a line break or using a non-linear scale without indicating it with appropriate tick marks.

instruction: Avoid high-contrast image adjustments that eliminate the background of blots or gels.
source_quote: photos of blots or gels should have contrast that does not eliminate the background, as such high contrast might hide light bands.

instruction: Separate regions from different micrographs or blots within one panel by white space, not lines.
source_quote: when regions of different micrographs or photos of blots make up a single panel, they should be separated by white space.

instruction: Explain image adjustments that selectively affect some regions or colors.
source_quote: Explain adjustments that selectively affect some regions or colors of the image

instruction: Write legends so figures stand alone without reference to the paper text.
source_quote: This text enables the figure to stand alone, so that the reader may understand it without reference to the text of the paper or proposal.

instruction: Include in the legend only the information needed to interpret the figure, leaving protocol details to the methods.
source_quote: Include only information in a legend necessary to interpret the figure

instruction: State the figure's result in the legend, ideally as its title.
source_quote: Thus, you should include it in the legend; making it the title is an effective way to emphasize the point of the figure.

instruction: Reserve interpretation of the figure for the title(s), not the legend body.
source_quote: Interpret the figure only in the title(s)

instruction: Make figure titles a single statement of the result so the figure stands alone.
source_quote: The title helps the figure stand alone by making clear what result it’s supposed to show.

instruction: Keep figure legends descriptive; do not interpret the results within the legend.
source_quote: the legend for A goes a bit beyond helping the figure stand alone by interpreting the results of JZL184 treatment.

instruction: Define specialized terms or drugs mentioned in a legend instead of leaving them unexplained.
source_quote: Perhaps the authors intended to explain the purpose of the drug, in which case they could have said what JZL184 is—an MAGL inhibitor.

instruction: Only mention error measures such as SEM if error bars are actually shown.
source_quote: The legend does appear to include a minor error in its mention of SEM, as no error bars are included on any of the graphs.

instruction: Label graph elements thoroughly so readers rarely need to consult the legend.
source_quote: they’re labeled thoroughly—almost no reference to the legend is required.

instruction: Display comparable data consistently across panels of the same figure.
source_quote: the data in A are displayed differently from those in B despite the fact that they’re both showing hydrolytic activity.

instruction: Prefer simple plot types, such as scatter plots, over bar graphs when they convey the result with less space.
source_quote: It’s unclear why a bar graph is necessary to show the effect of JZL184; a scatter plot would show equally well that the drug decreases activity and use much less space.

instruction: Do not reuse the same color for different meanings across panels of one figure.
source_quote: in A, red indicates treatment with JZL, while in B and C it indicates high-grade tumors.

instruction: Use the same axis scales for panels showing similar measurements so readers do not draw wrong comparisons.
source_quote: The most problematic inconsistency is the different scales for similar panels, as the reader may incorrectly conclude that tumors contain similar levels of C16:0 FFA as C18:0 FFA, when levels of C18:0 FFA are actually somewhat higher.

instruction: State the research question so it corresponds to the paper's conclusion.
source_quote: In a paper, make it correspond to the conclusion

instruction: Organize the introduction as problem, then unknown, then question.
source_quote: Organize: problem unknown question

instruction: Explain how the research addresses something unknown about an important problem.
source_quote: Explain why you did/ will do the research o How it relates to an important problem o How it addresses something unknown about the problem

instruction: Make the research question as specific as possible to the outcome of the research.
source_quote: the research question in a paper should not be vague or broad. Instead, it should be as specific as possible to the outcome of the research.

instruction: Compose the paper's question by starting from the conclusion, using similar terms and point of view.
source_quote: Now write the question that statement answers, using similar terms and point of view so that the reader can recognize that they correspond.

instruction: Avoid stating an overly broad question that the results will not solve.
source_quote: Stating an overly broad question or unknown at the beginning of the paper may lead the reader to believe that the results will solve it

instruction: Avoid limiting the question to only a few experiments, which leaves readers lost.
source_quote: limiting your question to something answered by a few of your experiments will fail to attract readers interested in the remaining ones

instruction: State the purpose of the work directly so readers can identify it.
source_quote: it’s much easier for the reader to identify it if you say it directly.

instruction: In a proposal, make the goal statement encompass all the aims.
source_quote: The statement of the purpose of the work should encompass all of the aims and make clear what the research will discover or find out.

instruction: Repeat the research question in the research strategy, in the significance part and/or to introduce each aim.
source_quote: it’s worth repeating in the research strategy section—in the significance part and/or to introduce each aim

instruction: Keep the paper consistent and telling a unified story.
source_quote: What’s more important is that the paper itself is consistent and tells a unified story

instruction: State an overall goal or hypothesis that covers all the aims and clarifies how they relate.
source_quote: Either start with an overall goal or write a goal that covers all the aims

instruction: Define the important problem as narrowly as possible.
source_quote: Define the important problem as narrowly as possible

instruction: State explicitly what is unknown about the problem.
source_quote: State what’s unknown about the problem

instruction: Avoid claiming novelty with risky words like "novel" or "first"; instead state the unknown directly.
source_quote: it directly identifies what’s novel about the project without using risky words like “novel” or “first”

instruction: Include only background needed to link the problem to the unknown and the unknown to the question.
source_quote: The only background an introduction needs is the same as that in a specific aims page (with a few more details and including references)—enough to link the problem to the unknown and the unknown to the question.

instruction: Avoid organizing the introduction as separate mini-reviews of topics.
source_quote: This approach generates a unified introduction, avoiding mini-reviews and awkward organization, such as the common “background on topic A, background on topic B” format.

instruction: Do not open with broad statements your audience already knows.
source_quote: Starting with the problem also helps avoid starting so broadly that you say something your audience already knows

instruction: Organize background logically to connect the problem to the question.
source_quote: Organize background to connect the problem to the question

instruction: Explain why the work excites you so readers share that excitement.
source_quote: The simplest way to get a reader excited is to explain why you’re excited (or why your mentor is excited)

instruction: Explain significance in terms of the big picture, such as opening new areas of discovery.
source_quote: Write about how your work will “open up a new area of discovery or develop new approaches to major problems”

instruction: Explain in the introduction why the research is worth doing.
source_quote: it still achieves the purpose of an introduction: it explains why the research is worth doing.

instruction: Give detailed background only about the most important piece of background so the introduction does not become too long.
source_quote: Another reason the extensive detail works in this intro is that details are only given about the most important piece of background, so it doesn’t make the section too long.

instruction: Deviate from the standard introduction formula only when the changes help explain why you did the work.
source_quote: Can deviate from formula if changes help explain why you did the work

instruction: Set up a controversy in the introduction rather than in a specific aims page.
source_quote: Set up a controversy in an introduction (not in specific aims)

instruction: Convince readers that the research was necessary to answer the question by including evidence for both possible outcomes.
source_quote: papers must convince readers (especially editors) that the research in the paper was necessary to answer the question. This paper does that by including evidence for both possible outcomes.

instruction: State specifically what is unknown in the field, matching what the paper actually does.
source_quote: it identifies what’s unknown, and does so very specifically

instruction: Follow the statement of the unknown with a question that corresponds closely to the conclusion in the abstract.
source_quote: the section follows the unknown with a statement of the question that corresponds closely to the conclusion in the abstract

instruction: Make the research question understandable even to readers outside the field.
source_quote: This inversion works because the question is understandable even to those outside the field

instruction: Mention methods only briefly at the end of the introduction.
source_quote: Mention methods only briefly

instruction: Do not describe the experimental setup in detail at the end of the introduction when the question already makes clear how it will be answered.
source_quote: The specificity of the question makes the detailed explanation of the setup of the experiment unnecessary.

instruction: State the overall conclusion at the very beginning of the discussion in a single, direct sentence.
source_quote: State the conclusion at the very beginning of the discussion

instruction: Summarize your findings in a single memorable sentence that is direct and brief.
source_quote: Summarize your findings in a single sentence

instruction: Limit speculation to one logical step beyond your conclusions and avoid suggesting experiments you don't want to do.
source_quote: Limit your speculation: one step, no experiments you don’t want to do

instruction: Explain how your important results relate to the field in general.
source_quote: Explain how important results relate to the field in general

instruction: Identify possible criticisms and explain why your conclusions still stand.
source_quote: Identify possible criticisms and explain why your conclusions still stand

instruction: Address inconsistencies within the paper and with others' results.
source_quote: Address inconsistencies within the paper and with others’ results

instruction: Explain why limitations of your methods don't disqualify your conclusions.
source_quote: Explain why limitations of methods don’t disqualify conclusions

instruction: Defend your interpretation by explaining why alternative conclusions are less likely.
source_quote: Defend your interpretation/ explain why others aren’t as likely

instruction: Indicate how you organized the material of your discussion.
source_quote: Indicate how you organized your material

instruction: Make claims of novelty indirectly to protect against overlooked literature.
source_quote: Claims of novelty must be indirect to protect against the possibility that the result exists in literature you haven’t read

instruction: Handle controversy carefully rather than avoiding it entirely.
source_quote: controversy must be handled carefully to avoid angering a reviewer whose work falls on the other side

instruction: Avoid organizing the discussion by the order results appeared, which tempts you to re-describe results.
source_quote: this organization is the trickiest, as it may make it hard to avoid describing the results again at the beginning of each paragraph

instruction: Avoid repeating too much of the results in the discussion.
source_quote: Avoid repeating too much of the results

instruction: Indicate how you organized the discussion to help the reader follow.
source_quote: Indicate how you organized to help the reader follow

instruction: Break the discussion into subsections with headings stating the main idea of each, if needed for coherence.
source_quote: you could avoid the problem altogether by breaking the discussion into subsections with headings that state the main idea of each

instruction: Explain how each topic relates to the previous topic or the overall conclusions.
source_quote: These indications of topics can be modified to explain how they relate to the previous topic or the overall conclusions.

instruction: Indicate how you decided what material belonged in which paragraph so readers see what connects the sentences.
source_quote: the key is to indicate how you decided what material belonged in which paragraph, as this helps the reader see what connects all the sentences in it

instruction: Open the discussion with the conclusions and what they mean, not with a restatement of results or a second introduction.
source_quote: This discussion starts with the conclusions and moves forward into what they mean, which is the point of a discussion but is still worth noting since so many discussions dwell on results or begin with a second introduction.

instruction: In the discussion, describe only results or aspects of results that do not appear earlier in the paper.
source_quote: Describe only results (or aspects of results) that don’t appear earlier

instruction: Use detailed descriptions of individual observations in the discussion only as evidence supporting new ideas not proposed earlier.
source_quote: these descriptions are either in greater detail than those in the results section or are not in the results at all, and each is used as evidence to support an idea not proposed earlier in the paper.

instruction: State the overall conclusion in the first paragraph of the discussion in the simplest, most direct way.
source_quote: However, the statement of the overall message is not the simplest, most memorable way to say it; “our results show that the experience of both positive and negative emotion persists despite impaired declarative memory for the inducing events” is a more direct alternative.

instruction: Write the first paragraph of the discussion about what the conclusions mean.
source_quote: Write the first paragraph about what the conclusions mean

instruction: Convey novelty by explaining how the conclusions relate to current understanding rather than by calling them novel.
source_quote: This helps emphasize how novel and exciting they are (without saying “novel”) and puts them in context; even someone outside the field can tell that this paper is an advance in the understanding of emotional memory.

instruction: Keep each discussion paragraph to a single focus; move specific results into their own paragraph.
source_quote: (The latter half of the paragraph is about a specific result and should probably be a separate paragraph.)

instruction: Compare your results with those of other investigators in the discussion.
source_quote: The first paragraph is the only one that even somewhat compares the results to others’, which leaves the reader to wonder whether the individual results, such as those on recollection in amnesic patients or induction of emotions by film clips, agree with those of other investigators.

instruction: Address potential reviewer concerns, such as apparent inconsistencies in methods, in the discussion.
source_quote: Failing to address potential reviewer concerns raises doubts

instruction: Limit speculation and give reasons for suggested possibilities so the reader can judge which is most likely.
source_quote: some of the speculation is rather open-ended—the second paragraph eliminates only one of four possible mechanisms the authors suggest. This doesn’t help the reader form an opinion about which is most likely, and seems almost inappropriate for a paper since the possibilities are given without reason for why they’re being suggested.

instruction: Frame speculative possibilities with observations as conditions, not possibilities as conditions.
source_quote: this and the other speculative part are appropriately limited, taking observations as the condition for each possibility (not a possibility as the condition).

instruction: Explain the relevance of the findings beyond the field, to the real world.
source_quote: Explain relevance beyond the field

instruction: Avoid overstating the importance of the findings with examples that go beyond what is necessary.
source_quote: The second reason, with its mention of a popular movie, may go further than necessary to establish importance since memory erasure is not currently a common occurrence.

instruction: Include the results in the abstract.
source_quote: The part that an abstract obviously must include is the results—the payoff for all your hard work and what determines the potential impact of your paper.

instruction: State the important problem your work addresses in the abstract.
source_quote: One way to address this is to state the problem your work addresses; another is to say what they mean for the broader field—their implications.

instruction: Explain how your work relates to the big picture and why it matters.
source_quote: How does your work relate to the big picture—why does it matter to science or human health?

instruction: State the implications of your findings for the broader field.
source_quote: Including both would best show why editors and other scientists should care, especially if the implications are clear and direct.

instruction: Put the important problem at the beginning of the abstract.
source_quote: Since the important problem is at the beginning of the story, they’re especially effective—they can grab a reader’s attention with the importance of your work.

instruction: Connect the problem to the results with a clear logical step.
source_quote: We need another step in the authors’ logic

instruction: State the research question in the abstract.
source_quote: The key piece that would answer this question is what the authors were trying to find out when they started the work—their research question.

instruction: Include the key parts of the introduction, results, and discussion in the abstract.
source_quote: In an abstract, this generally requires the most important pieces of the important sections (introduction, results, and discussion).

instruction: Include the problem, the path from problem to question, and the question from the introduction.
source_quote: The key parts of the introduction are the problem, how you got from the problem to the question, and the question

instruction: Describe what you did and what you found in the abstract.
source_quote: those in the results are, of course, what you did and what you found

instruction: Include the conclusion and, if significant, the implication for health or future research.
source_quote: the discussion’s highlights are the conclusion and, if it’s significant, the implication for health or future research.

instruction: Revise an abstract assembled from the paper so it reads coherently.
source_quote: such a collage-style abstract may not automatically read smoothly—it will likely need some revision for coherence

instruction: Make the abstract short enough to meet the journal's length limit.
source_quote: it will likely be longer than the journal allows, so you’ll need to make it shorter

instruction: Write the abstract so readers can decide whether to read the whole paper.
source_quote: An obvious function of an abstract is to provide the reader with enough information to allow him or her to decide whether to read the whole paper.

instruction: Define terms before using them in the abstract.
source_quote: define terms before using them, and frame results and conclusions so that they clearly correspond to the question.

instruction: Frame results and conclusions so they clearly correspond to the research question.
source_quote: frame results and conclusions so that they clearly correspond to the question.

instruction: Avoid overly detailed statements of results in the abstract.
source_quote: the statements of the results are too detailed, and it’s hard to see how they address the question.

instruction: Use a unifying framing concept to keep the abstract coherent.
source_quote: The authors’ decision to frame everything in terms of competition unifies the final version of the abstract.

instruction: Explain the rationale in the specific aims, including the problem, the unknown, and the overall goal.
source_quote: Rationale includes problem, unknown, and overall goal

instruction: Explain thoroughly how your work relates to the problem, taking up a considerable proportion of the aims page.
source_quote: How your work relates to the problem  Explain as thoroughly as possible  Will take up considerable proportion of aims page

instruction: Explain how your work relates to a significant problem to which the funding agency is devoted.
source_quote: explaining how your work relates to a significant problem to which the funding agency is devoted

instruction: Explain the relationship of your project to the funding institution’s goals.
source_quote: Explain the relationship of your project to the funding institution’s goals

instruction: Show that your results will be novel rather than unsurprising.
source_quote: they’ll also want to be sure that your results will be novel—if they’re unsurprising, the research isn’t really worth doing.

instruction: Do not spend most of the specific aims space restating hypotheses and describing your qualifications.
source_quote: this explanation is more important than what the authors spend most of their space on (see part 2—re-stating their hypotheses and describing their qualifications to do the research)

instruction: State directly what makes your research innovative.
source_quote: Stating directly what makes your research innovative, as in the (unaltered) remainder of the Aims considered above, will help make a case for the impact of your work

instruction: Focus on the proposed research rather than on what you have already done.
source_quote: Focus on the proposed research, not what you’ve already done

instruction: Keep the aims centered on the big picture rather than devolving into a list of methods.
source_quote: The lack of detail about their experiments helps to keep the aims centered on the goals and hypotheses rather than devolving into a list of methods.

instruction: Include methods only if they are innovative, and explain how they differ from conventional methods and why they work better.
source_quote: you should not only say what you will do, but explain how it’s different from conventional methods and why it works better for your project than other possible methods.

instruction: Omit nonessential parts when shortening a summary.
source_quote: Omit nonessential parts

instruction: Combine sentences by pairing the method as subject with the result as completer.
source_quote: Combine sentences o Method (subject) + result (completer)

instruction: Make sentences more direct by making the action the verb.
source_quote: Make sentences more direct o Make the action the verb

instruction: Condense or omit the less essential parts first, such as details of methods and minor results.
source_quote: The parts that are likely least important for getting published or funded are the details of the research—the methods and minor results.

instruction: Omit the method if it is obvious from the aim or the result.
source_quote: If the method is obvious from the aim or the result, you don’t need

instruction: Omit results that are not essential to the conclusion.
source_quote: not every result is essential to the conclusion, so you may need to leave some of them out. To decide which to keep, rank them by how exciting or necessary to support the conclusion they are and keep as many as will fit.

instruction: Combine background with the unknown, or a method with its result, into one sentence.
source_quote: You may be able to combine a piece of background information with the statement of the unknown, or a method with the result it yielded. In such a sentence, the method becomes the subject and the verb the completer

instruction: Make sentences direct by using the verb to convey the action.
source_quote: To shorten sentences, the most effective approach is to make them more direct by using the verb to convey the action—this will eliminate verbs that don’t do anything in the sentence

instruction: Use a verb in the title to state the result of the work.
source_quote: a list of topics sounds rather flat and unexciting, and a title should attract editors’ and reviewers’ attention—you need a verb. A verb will let you state the result or expected result of your work

instruction: State your conclusion directly in the title.
source_quote: State your conclusion directly in the title

instruction: Put the broadest, most important concept at the beginning of the title.
source_quote: The structure of the title matters—whatever’s at the beginning is what the paper or proposal is about

instruction: State the paper's central message as your conclusion before writing.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: In a paper, the message is your conclusion—what all your results allow you to say that you couldn't have said before you did the experiments

instruction: Make the message statement as accurate, powerful, and direct as possible.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Statement of message should be as accurate, powerful, and direct as possible

instruction: Ensure the message statement reflects all important results or aims.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Since this one statement will shape the whole document, it's important that it reflects all of your important results or all of your aims.

instruction: Avoid hedging words like 'may' or 'could' in the message statement.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Your reader likely won't believe that you can accomplish your goal, or have demonstrated your conclusion, if the statement of it includes "may" or "could."

instruction: Write the message as a simple sentence stating one idea in as few words as possible.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Easy-tounderstand sentences are generally simple: they state one idea in as few words as possible.

instruction: Plan each section's arguments, evidence, and organization before writing.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: The second is planning how to convey that in each of the sections—what arguments you will make, what evidence you will use to support them, and how all of the ideas will be organized.

instruction: Revise the message statement repeatedly until it cannot be improved.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Draft and revise, revise, revise

instruction: Distinguish new findings from what is already known when composing the message.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Maybe there's something in there that we don't need to say—let's consider what's already known

instruction: Place the most important distinction at the beginning of the message sentence.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: That distinction is important, so let's place it at the beginning

instruction: Remove verbs that do not add meaning to make sentences more direct.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: There are an awful lot of verbs in there, and not all of them add meaning.

instruction: Group closely related ideas together so that all material on the same topic appears in the same paragraph or subsection.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: This map indicates the organization of the section: all of the material on each topic will be in the same subsection, which may be one or several paragraphs, depending on the degree of branching.

instruction: Give each paragraph a single topic, and make items that belong to no group their own paragraph if you can elaborate on them.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: If it doesn’t belong with anything else, it should be its own paragraph, as long as you can elaborate on it.

instruction: Support each main idea with at least two pieces of evidence or argument.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Each heading should have at least two supporting pieces.

instruction: Write main ideas in a consistent grammatical format to improve the continuity of the text.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Composing all of these in the same format (all sentences, or all infinitive phrases) will improve the continuity of the resulting text.

instruction: Order topics so that transitions between them are easy to write.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: Deciding on the order may be more complex, requiring you to think ahead to how you might write transitions between topics—the order in which transitions are easier to imagine will work best.

instruction: In a discussion, brainstorm alternative interpretations, possible mechanisms, and implications for the broader field as topics.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: If you’re planning a discussion, these topics might be alternative interpretations, possible mechanisms underlying your observations, and implications for the broader field.

instruction: Revise your plan if it stops helping you write; prioritize logical, clear writing over following the plan.
source_file: .writing_guides/general/7 Getting started on a paper or proposal.pdf
source_quote: In this case, revise the plan— there’s no reason to stick to it if it doesn’t help you write. Making your writing logical and clear is more important than following a set of steps.

instruction: Make each paragraph a single unit of thought or one logical step in the argument.
source_quote: A paragraph is a unit of thought or a logical step in an argument

instruction: Use reverse outlining to check that your writing is organized into paragraphs.
source_quote: If you’re not sure that your writing is organized into paragraphs, try reverse outlining

instruction: Break up a paragraph if its summary requires more than one clause.
source_quote: Summarize each paragraph  If a summary requires more than one clause, it should be broken up

instruction: Combine paragraphs whose summaries are the same.
source_quote: Compare summaries  If two summaries are the same, the paragraphs should be combined

instruction: Put related paragraphs together so each builds logically on the previous one.
source_quote: Re-order paragraphs  Put related paragraphs together  Each builds logically on the previous one

instruction: Decide sentence order within a paragraph by the relationships among sentences.
source_quote: Rearrange material into unified paragraphs  Decide sentence order by relationships among sentences

instruction: Revise for reader ease after reorganizing.
source_quote: Revise for reader ease after reorganizing

instruction: Write unified paragraphs that are all about one thing.
source_quote: paragraphs should be unified (all about one thing)

instruction: Group sentences that address the same topic together in the same paragraph.
source_quote: it concerns the overall problem of sponsor control of clinical trials, so it should be grouped with the other sentences on that

instruction: After reorganizing sentences, revise them so their relationships to one another are clear.
source_quote: After reorganizing, revise to make the sentences relate to one another more clearly

instruction: When deciding paragraph topics, think about the aim of the section or document as a whole and how each sentence relates to it.
source_quote: it will help to think about the aim of the section or document as a whole and determine how your sentences relate to that

instruction: Use judgment when ordering sentences, considering how each relates to the whole.
source_quote: Use judgment and think about how the sentences relate to the whole

instruction: Write new sentences if a point needs support that existing sentences do not provide.
source_quote: you need to write new ones to support a point you hadn’t realized was so important as you were drafting

instruction: Give each sentence a clear purpose within its paragraph so its position is justified.
source_quote: we would need to change the sentence itself to make clear how it relates to those sentences and why the authors bring up the point

instruction: Reorder paragraphs so they follow a logical progression of related ideas.
source_quote: The next step in reverse outlining is to order the paragraphs by their relatedness and where they fit in the logical progression.

instruction: Group together paragraphs whose ideas are similar.
source_quote: To determine which paragraphs should be grouped together, ask which of these paragraph summaries are most related.

instruction: Place descriptive paragraphs near the beginning of an argument.
source_quote: Descriptions seem to work better as introductions to an argument, suggesting that 4 and 8 may belong at the beginning.

instruction: Use a suggestion for change as the conclusion of the argument.
source_quote: The suggestion for change works well as a conclusion, so we arrive at the following organization:

instruction: Rewrite sentences after reordering them to strengthen the connections between them.
source_quote: you may need to do more re-writing of the sentences themselves after you re-order them (as with sentence 6) to strengthen the connections.

instruction: Try multiple arrangements of sentences and choose the one that works best.
source_quote: try multiple arrangements of sentences to see which works best to you.

instruction: Be prepared to delete or add material when reorganizing paragraphs.
source_quote: May need a lot of change (even deleting or adding material)

instruction: Keep paragraphs on the same topic distinct from those on other topics, such as separating education-related points from research-related ones.
source_quote: Since 9 concerns education rather than research, it should lie outside the group of 1, 6, and 10.

instruction: Focus the paper on a single central contribution and communicate it in the title.
source_quote: Focus on a single message; papers that simultaneously focus on multiple contributions tend to be less convincing about each and are therefore less memorable.

instruction: Write for readers who do not know your work.
source_quote: Write for flesh-and-blood human beings who do not know your work

instruction: Define technical terms clearly.
source_quote: Define technical terms clearly because readers can become frustrated when they encounter a word that they don’t understand.

instruction: Avoid abbreviations and acronyms.
source_quote: Avoid abbreviations and acronyms so that readers do not have to go back to earlier sections to identify them.

instruction: Minimize the number of loose threads the reader must keep in mind.
source_quote: Do your best to minimize the number of loose threads that the reader has to keep in mind at any one time.

instruction: Keep the reader in mind constantly while writing.
source_quote: When you write, you should constantly have your reader in mind.

instruction: Make the scientific logic supporting your claim crystal clear.
source_quote: your scientific logic must be crystal clear to powerfully make your claim

instruction: Hone the title early and regularly while writing.
source_quote: Thinking about the title early—and regularly returning to hone it—can help not only the writing of the paper but also the process of designing experiments or developing theories.

instruction: Structure the paper using the context-content-conclusion scheme at whole-paper, section, and paragraph scales.
source_quote: Rule 3: Stick to the context-content-conclusion (C-C-C) scheme

instruction: Set the context in the introduction, present content in the results, and deliver the conclusion in the discussion.
source_quote: At the wholepaper scale, the introduction sets the context, the results are the content, and the discussion brings home the conclusion.

instruction: Begin each paragraph with a topic sentence, put novel content in the body, and end with a concluding sentence.
source_quote: Applying C-C-C at the paragraph scale, the first sentence defines the topic or context, the body hosts the novel content put forth for the reader’s consideration, and the last sentence provides the conclusion to be remembered.

instruction: Do not structure the paper chronologically around your research activities; reorganize the material around the claim and its supporting logic.
source_quote: They do not care about the chronological path by which you reached a result; they just care about the ultimate claim and the logic supporting it

instruction: Cover each subject in only one place, except for the central idea, to minimize subject changes.
source_quote: Only the central idea of the paper should be touched upon multiple times. Otherwise, each subject should be covered in only one place in order to minimize the number of subject changes.

instruction: Keep related sentences and paragraphs together without interrupting them with unrelated material.
source_quote: Related sentences or paragraphs should be strung together rather than interrupted by unrelated material. Ideas that are similar, such as two reasons why we should believe something, should come one immediately after the other.

instruction: Use parallel form for parallel messages across consecutive sentences or paragraphs.
source_quote: Similarly, across consecutive paragraphs or sentences, parallel messages should be communicated with parallel form.

instruction: Make the abstract convey the complete message of the paper.
source_quote: Rule 5: Tell a complete story in the abstract

instruction: Open the abstract with broad context, narrow to the specific gap, then present the approach, results, and conclusion.
source_quote: The first sentence orients the reader by introducing the broader field in which the particular research is situated. Then, this context is narrowed until it lands on the open question that the research answered.

instruction: In the abstract, describe the novel method or approach before presenting the results.
source_quote: The content (“Here we”) first describes the novel method or approach that you used to fill the gap or question. Then you present the meat—your executive summary of the results.

instruction: End the abstract by interpreting the results to answer the question posed in the context, and state the broader significance.
source_quote: Finally, the conclusion interprets the results to answer the question that was posed at the end of the context section. There is often a second part to the conclusion section that highlights how this conclusion moves the broader field forward (i.e., “broader significance”).

instruction: Do not present results in the abstract before establishing the context the reader needs to understand them.
source_quote: This structure helps you avoid the most common mistake with the abstract, which is to talk about results before the reader is ready to understand them.

instruction: Communicate in the introduction why the paper matters by highlighting the gap in current knowledge or methods.
source_quote: Rule 6: Communicate why the paper matters in the introduction The introduction highlights the gap that exists in current knowledge or methods and why it is important.

instruction: Build the introduction through progressively more specific paragraphs ending in a gap statement, then a paragraph on what the paper does to fill it.
source_quote: This is usually done by a set of progressively more specific paragraphs that culminate in a clear exposition of what is lacking in the literature, followed by a paragraph summarizing what the paper does to fill that gap.

instruction: Keep the introduction free of broad literature review beyond the paper's motivation.
source_quote: The introduction should not contain a broad literature review beyond the motivation of the paper.

instruction: Use the last paragraph of the introduction to compactly summarize the results.
source_quote: The last paragraph of the introduction is special: it compactly summarizes the results, which fill the gap you just established.

instruction: Present results as a sequence of logically connected statements supporting the central contribution.
source_quote: Deliver the results as a sequence of statements, supported by figures, that connect logically to support the central contribution

instruction: Make figure titles state the conclusion of the analysis and legends explain how it was done.
source_quote: the title of the figure should communicate the conclusion of the analysis, and the legend should explain how it was done.

instruction: Start each results paragraph with a sentence or two setting up the question it answers.
source_quote: Each subsequent paragraph in the results section starts with a sentence or two that set up the question that the paragraph answers

instruction: End each results paragraph with a sentence that answers the question it posed.
source_quote: the paragraph ends with a sentence that answers the question.

instruction: Begin the first results paragraph with a summary of the overall approach and key innovative methods.
source_quote: The first results paragraph is special in that it typically summarizes the overall approach to the problem outlined in the introduction, along with any key innovative methods that were developed.

instruction: Use the discussion to explain how the gap was filled, note limitations, and describe relevance to the field.
source_quote: Discuss how the gap was filled, the limitations of the interpretation, and the relevance to the field

instruction: Start the discussion with a paragraph summarizing the important findings.
source_quote: The first discussion paragraph is special in that it generally summarizes the important findings from the results section.

instruction: Open each subsequent discussion paragraph with an area of weakness or strength and evaluate it against the literature.
source_quote: Each of the following paragraphs in the discussion section starts by describing an area of weakness or strength of the paper. It then evaluates the strength or weakness by linking it to the relevant literature.

instruction: Give each paragraph a defined role in advancing the story, scrutinized at the outline stage.
source_quote: Because the story has an overall arc, each paragraph should have a defined role in advancing this story.

instruction: Seek feedback from test readers and colleagues to verify that the paper's story works.
source_quote: Successfully writing a paper typically requires input from multiple people. Test readers are necessary to make sure that the overall story works.

instruction: Be willing to discard and rewrite whole paragraphs rather than editing incrementally.
source_quote: In many cases, trashing entire paragraphs and rewriting is a faster way to produce good text than incremental editing.

instruction: Ensure you can describe the paper's full outline in a few minutes; otherwise distill the story further.
source_quote: if you, as the writer, cannot describe the entire outline of a paper to a colleague in a few minutes, then clearly a reader will not be able to. You need to further distill your story.

instruction: Address unanswered criticisms and questions in the discussion.
source_quote: 8: Discussion: Preempt criticism, give future impact Readers are left with unanswered criticisms and/or questions on their mind.

instruction: Make the introduction convey why the paper matters to generate reader interest.
source_quote: 6: Introduction: Why the paper matters Readers show little interest in the paper.

instruction: Master the standard structural rules before creatively bending them.
source_quote: a thorough mastery of the standard rules is necessary to successfully bend them

instruction: Write the truth; do not distort or hide facts.
source_quote: 1. Сила - в правде

instruction: Prioritize meaning over form.
source_quote: 2. Смысл важнее формы

instruction: Prefer simpler wording wherever possible.
source_quote: 3. Чем проще - тем лучше

instruction: Write as if for yourself, the reader.
source_quote: 4. Пишите, как для себя

instruction: Read your text aloud to check it.
source_quote: 5. Читайте вслух

instruction: Support statements with examples.
source_quote: 6. Приводите примеры

instruction: Move from simple material to complex.
source_quote: 7. От простого к сложному

instruction: Put the benefit to the reader first.
source_quote: 8. Пользу- вперед

instruction: Give the text a heading.
source_quote: 9. Поставьте заголовок

instruction: Show respect and care toward the reader.
source_quote: 10. Уважение и забота

instruction: Cut filler words and keep the text concise.
source_quote: Как излагать мысли кратко, ясно и убедительно, без языкового мусора, фальши и штампов.

instruction: Avoid clichés and officialese; write plainly and concretely.
source_quote: Горячая вода отключена с 1 по 13 мая.

instruction: Explain the reasons behind decisions so readers understand the necessity.
source_quote: А еще это объявление наконец-то объясняет, что отключение воды - не прихоть садистов- коммунальщиков, а необходимость.

instruction: Be honest and direct even when the message is unpleasant.
source_quote: От текста справа больнее, но он честный и прямой.

instruction: Write so that readers understand you and act on your text.
source_quote: от того, как мы формулируем мысли на письме, зависит очень многое: понимают нас или нет, прислушиваются ли к нам, делают ли другие то, что нам нужно

instruction: Write briefly, without unnecessary words, but without losing meaning.
source_quote: Кратко - то есть без лишних слов, но не в ущерб смыслу.

instruction: Write clearly so the reader understands the thought immediately, without decoding.
source_quote: Ясно - то есть так, чтобы мысль была понятна сразу, а не после расшифровки.

instruction: Write convincingly so readers listen to you and act with you.
source_quote: Убедительно - то есть так, чтобы люди к вам прислушивались и действовали с вами заодно.

instruction: Seek the truth and avoid subjective evaluations, letting readers draw their own conclusions.
source_quote: В информационном стиле приходится искать правду, отказываться от необъективных оценок и помогать читателю самостоятельно делать выводы.

instruction: Write simply, even at the cost of sounding respectable.
source_quote: Информационный стиль заставляет писать просто, даже в ущерб статусу и респектабельности

instruction: Tell the uncomfortable truth instead of smoothing over problems.
source_quote: Информационный стиль ставит правду на первое место, даже если она неудобная. Даже если все вокруг просят сгладить углы.

instruction: Avoid overloaded and ambiguous sentences.
source_quote: Информационный стиль борется с перегруженностью и двусмысленностью.

instruction: Support claims with facts instead of stretched arguments.
source_quote: Там, где обычно автор может извернуться и притянуть аргументы за уши, в информационном стиле должны стоять факты.

instruction: Do not distort facts to fit the story you want to tell.
source_quote: Хочется рассказать одну историю, а факты говорят об обратном

instruction: Remove superfluous words from sentences and superfluous sentences from paragraphs.
source_quote: В предложении не должно быть ненужных слов, в абзаце – ненужных предложений, так же, как и на картине не должно быть ненужных штрихов, а в механизме - ненужных частей

instruction: Avoid clichés, officialese and dead formal constructions.
source_quote: В ее книге «Слово живое и мертвое» собраны примеры борьбы со штампами, канцеляритом и мертвыми формальными конструкциями.

instruction: Avoid empty, meaningless phrases that hide the substance.
source_quote: Он помогает вытравить пустословие и обнажить суть в любом тексте

instruction: Persuade without manipulation, pressure or deception.
source_quote: Эта книга об убеждении без грязных манипуляций, давления и обмана.

instruction: Organize your thinking first; a clear text follows from an ordered mind.
source_quote: Эта книга о порядке в голове. Когда есть порядок в голове, порядок в тексте приходит сам собой.

instruction: Prefer simple honest words over pompous phrases.
source_quote: О том, как напыщенные фразы меркнут рядом с простыми честными словами.

instruction: Focus on meaningful content instead of decorating simple facts with ornate, formulaic language.
source_quote: смысл всегда важнее слов

instruction: Remove meaningless verbal embellishments that add no information.
source_quote: мы избавляем текст от бессмысленной мишуры и помогаем авторам рассказать о важном

instruction: Write briefly, clearly and convincingly.
source_quote: информационный стиль поможет донести это кратко, интересно и убедительно

instruction: Do not rely on special or ritual words to make a text work; they have no power apart from meaning.
source_quote: Культ слов - это вера в то, что определенные слова обладают волшебной силой в отрыве от смысла

instruction: Do not use empty exclamatory flourishes and clichés that admire form rather than convey content.
source_quote: это всё восхищение формой, а не содержанием

instruction: Clean the text at the word level by finding and deleting verbal garbage.
source_quote: Вы узнаете о словесном мусоре: как его находить и удалять

instruction: Organize paragraphs so the reader quickly finds what they need.
source_quote: От предложений перейдем к абзацам: как их организовать, чтобы читатель быстро находил то, что ему нужно

instruction: Structure the text and its logic of presentation so a large article is easy and interesting to read.
source_quote: поговорим о структуре текста и логике изложения

instruction: Make sentences easy to read.
source_quote: Во второй главе переходим от слов к предложениям: как сделать так, чтобы их было легко читать

instruction: Do not expect style to fix a weak idea; ensure there is something meaningful to say first.
source_quote: Слабая мысль в инфостиле не станет сильной

instruction: Write with the reader's needs in mind, addressing a problem the reader wants solved.
source_quote: Главное в сильном тексте – забота о читателе.

instruction: Focus the text on the reader's tasks rather than the author's tasks.
source_quote: Статьи, написанные с учетом задач читателя, будут всегда сильнее и интереснее, чем статья о задачах автора.

instruction: Make sure the text is useful to the reader before writing it.
source_quote: Чтобы текст стал сильным, начните с того, чтобы он был зачем-то полезен читателю. Просто текст никому не нужен, даже красивый.

instruction: Be honest with the reader and speak about problems directly.
source_quote: Автор должен всегда быть честным перед читателем, предупреждать проблемы и не бояться прямо о них говорить.

instruction: Simplify the text wherever possible without losing meaning.
source_quote: Если текст можно упростить, его следует упростить.

instruction: Never express a thought more complexly than necessary, even for expert audiences.
source_quote: Нет ни одной ситуации, когда одну и ту же мысль стоит выражать сложнее, а не проще.

instruction: Remove stop-words that carry no meaning.
source_quote: На уровне слов мы удаляем из текста языковой мусор - слова, которые не несут смысла. Мы называем их стоп-словами

instruction: Simplify sentence syntax, the way words are connected within sentences.
source_quote: На уровне предложений мы упрощаем синтаксис - то, как слова связаны внутри предложения

instruction: Remove repetitions, redundancy and unnecessary details at the level of meaning.
source_quote: На уровне смысла мы избавляемся от повторов, избыточности и лишних деталей

instruction: Remove stop-words that can be deleted without losing meaning.
source_quote: Стоп-слова - это такие слова и фразы, которые удаляются из текста без потери смысла.

instruction: Replace evaluative words with facts that prove the evaluation.
source_quote: вместо оценок в тексте лучше ставить факты. Не «качественный», а «Сделан на таком-то заводе». Не «прочный», а «выдерживает падение с десятого этажа».

instruction: After deleting stop-words, add useful information so the text does not become dry and uninteresting.
source_quote: Редактура стоп-слов - это не просто удаление слов. Это еще и наполнение текста полезной информацией. Если забыть об этом, текст будет пересушенным и неинтересным.

instruction: Do not use all the formal possibilities of Russian syntax when simple expression suffices.
source_quote: авторам не рекомендуется, как бы они того ни хотели, намеренно использовать все возможности русского синтаксиса, структуры предложений, системы однородных членов и сложных предложений, чтобы ясно и просто выразить свои мысли, если того не требуют обстоятельства.

instruction: Avoid participles and passive voice when they hinder understanding.
source_quote: да, страдательный залог - это прекрасно. Но когда он мешает понимать текст, мы лучше обойдемся без него.

instruction: Do not use complex sentences or homogeneous members unless they help express the thought.
source_quote: Если сложные предложения или однородные члены не помогают выразить мысль, их не стоит употреблять.

instruction: Keep language means subordinate to simplicity and clarity.
source_quote: Средства языка не должны мешать простоте и ясности.

instruction: Remove introductory constructions that add no information.
source_quote: вводные слова не дают полезной информации, а зря занимают место на странице

instruction: Do not present claims as universally known; either delete them or explain the source.
source_quote: Фразы вроде «всем известно» и «Не секрет» - это ловушка. Если что-то и так известно, то об этом незачем писать

instruction: Do not emphasize that a statement is your opinion unless contrasting it with someone else's.
source_quote: Подчеркивать, что это ваше мнение, следует только в одном случае - когда вы противопоставляете свое мнение чужому

instruction: Avoid conversational hedges like «честно говоря» and «признаться».
source_quote: Аналогично с фразами вроде «честно говоря», «признаться» и «по правде сказать»

instruction: Avoid clarifying insertions like «вернее», «другими словами», «точнее»; state it precisely the first time.
source_quote: Еще из разговорной речи пришли уточняющие вводные: «вернее», «другими словами», «точнее». Но если вы можете сказать точнее, почему бы сразу так не сказать?

instruction: Do not number thoughts with words like «во-первых»; use paragraphs instead.
source_quote: Но на письме эти слова избыточны. Не нумеруйте мысли словами. Разбивайте их на абзацы: один абзац - одна мысль.

instruction: Use numbering only for step-by-step instructions or lists that will be referenced later.
source_quote: Нумерация нужна только тогда, когда вы пишете пошаговую инструкцию или на пункты вашего перечня нужно будет позже сослаться.

instruction: Avoid numbering where numbers do not add clarity.
source_quote: Старайтесь избегать нумерации там, где числа не добавляют ясности.

instruction: Remove the word «например» where a colon or context already signals an example.
source_quote: Но само слово «например» почти всегда избыточное

instruction: Do not cast the reader in unpleasant or potentially offensive hypothetical situations.
source_quote: Старайтесь не примерять на читателя неприятные или потенциально оскорбительные ситуации - даже гипотетические.

instruction: Show genuine care for the reader instead of formulaic politeness words.
source_quote: Подлинная вежливость проявляется не в словах, а во внимании и заботе о читателе.

instruction: Do not use «кстати» to attach off-topic text.
source_quote: Если что-то пришлось кстати, не надо это специально выделять. А если оно некстати, то никакое «кстати» ему не поможет.

instruction: Remove parenthetical content or integrate it into the sentence.
source_quote: Всё, что стоит в скобках, всем своим видом показывает, что это что-то неважное. Либо убирайте, либо доставайте из скобок

instruction: Check paired commas, dashes and parentheses near sentence starts for removable insertions.
source_quote: Чтобы научиться видеть в тексте вводные, смотрите на запятые, тире и скобки. Если они парные или стоят близко к началу предложения - это тревожный сигнал.

instruction: Read the text aloud; if you run out of breath or tangle intonation, split the sentence and remove insertions.
source_quote: Если не хватило воздуха, чтобы дочитать предложение до конца, - оно слишком сложное. Если запутались в интонациях - тоже слишком сложное.

instruction: Do not use introductory words and phrases such as "конечно", "очевидно", "как известно".
source_quote: Примеры вводных слов и словосочетаний без сомнения безусловно бесспорно более того

instruction: Avoid evaluative words; give facts instead so readers draw their own conclusions.
source_quote: Отказаться от оценок

instruction: Always give the reader information they can understand and evaluate themselves.
source_quote: Чтобы читатель поверил в оценку или сделал собственные выводы, мы должны дать ему опору: информацию, которую он поймет и сможет самостоятельно оценить.

instruction: Always provide facts, stories or examples so readers can evaluate the subject themselves.
source_quote: Всегда давайте людям что-то, чтобы они сами оценивали нужные вам предметы. Факты, истории, примеры - сгодится всё.

instruction: Treat every adjective with suspicion; beware of ones carrying subjective evaluation.
source_quote: Относитесь подозрительно к любому прилагательному. Если оно несет необъективную оценку - насторожитесь.

instruction: Never use quotation marks to convey irony or sarcasm.
source_quote: Не используйте кавычки для иронии или сарказма. Хотите иронию - подайте ее более эффектными средствами.

instruction: Choose neutral words over evaluative ones when naming the subject of discussion.
source_quote: Часто оценка заложена в том, какое мы используем слово для обозначения предмета разговора

instruction: Replace or supplement evaluative statements with facts that the reader can understand.
source_quote: Чтобы оценка стала убедительной, замените или дополните ее фактами. Факты должны быть понятными читателю. Если непонятны - поясняйте

instruction: Explain vague evaluations with concrete details instead of assuming the reader will understand.
source_quote: Он подумал, что отделается одним словом об экологичности: будто достаточно его сказать, и все сразу поймут, что он имел в виду. Но так не работает. Чтобы читатель понял, придется объяснить

instruction: Base every text on research and facts, otherwise it is empty talk.
source_quote: Создавать такой текст трудно, потому что автору придется разобраться в теме, изучить технические документы, почитать отраслевую прессу и поговорить с производителем. Это большая часть работы над текстом, и без нее ничего не получится. Без исследования и фактов любой текст - пустой трёп.

instruction: Avoid evaluative adjectives such as those listed in the guide's examples.
source_quote: Примеры оценок авторитетный активный актуальный астрономический аутентичный

instruction: Do not stack intensifiers on top of evaluations; use facts instead.
source_quote: Усилитель - оценка, наложенная на другую оценку: максимально выгодные условия очень качественное обслуживание абсолютно бесплатно

instruction: Let readers draw strong conclusions themselves by presenting facts rather than superlative words.
source_quote: Самые сильные убеждения - те, к которым читатель приходит самостоятельно. Помогите ему самому решить, что ваш товар «очень» или «самый». Но не пишите эти слова, а подбирайте факты.

instruction: Instead of praising a product in general terms, describe concrete situations where it is useful.
source_quote: В рекламе вместо положительных оценок полезно рассказывать о ситуациях, когда ваш продукт окажется полезен. Не говорите, что товар прекрасен - расскажите, когда он прекраснее всего

instruction: Tell stories and give examples with credible details instead of evaluations.
source_quote: Сила сценария в том, что он создает в голове человека реалистичный и понятный кинофильм. Нужно лишь подобрать достоверные детали, и вам больше не нужны оценки.

instruction: When evaluations help explain complex facts, combine facts with evaluations.
source_quote: Иногда оценки помогают понять сложные факты - например, у технически сложных приборов. В таком случае можно сделать факты вместе с оценками.

instruction: Не используйте усилители без доказательств — подкрепляйте сильные утверждения фактами.
source_quote: Как и оценки, усилители создают ложное чувство выполненной работы: вроде написал, какой у тебя замечательный продукт, но на самом деле ничего не сказал. Поэтому усилитель - ничто без доказательства.

instruction: Замените усилители конкретными фактами и доказательствами.
source_quote: Написать усилитель проще, чем доказательство. Чтобы доказать свою мысль, придется разыскать информацию, поговорить с экспертом, разобраться в теме и упаковать это всё с пользой для читателя.

instruction: Не называйте людей или продукты «настоящими» — расскажите вместо этого историю или приведите факты.
source_quote: Человек или товар не станут более настоящими, если их так называть. Зато, если вместо слова «настоящий» рассказать историю, получится интересно и убедительно

instruction: Избегайте перечисленных усилителей в тексте.
source_quote: Примеры усилителей абсолютно безоговорочно безусловно бесспорно весьма во всех отношениях вообще вполне всего лишь действительно довольно довольно-таки именно истинно, подлинно лишь максимально минимально

instruction: Избегайте штампов — устойчивых избитых выражений, которые делают текст неинформативным.
source_quote: Штамп - это популярное устойчивое словосочетание, смысл которого либо неясен, либо можно выразить одним словом.

instruction: Не перегружайте текст штампами, иначе читатель потеряет интерес.
source_quote: Если текст перегружен штампами, читатель быстро потеряет интерес. Он почувствует, что автор здесь налил водички, ничего стоящего в тексте не будет.

instruction: Замените штампы одним точным словом.
source_quote: Штамп обозначает одно слово, но выражается несколькими:

instruction: Избегайте газетных штампов из печатных и онлайновых СМИ.
source_quote: Газетные штампы пришли из печатных и онлайновых СМИ. Неопытные журналисты заучивают их, чтобы звучать профессионально. Но в языке такие штампы выглядят нелепо

instruction: Опирайтесь на факты, а не на владение штампами.
source_quote: Но настоящий журналист - не тот, кто владеет штампами, а тот, кто владеет фактами

instruction: Начинайте текст сразу с сути, без вводных прелюдий.
source_quote: Сразу к делу, без соплей и прелюдий.

instruction: Write without pretty phrases and clichés.
source_quote: Эта задача решается без красивых фраз и штампов.

instruction: State your thoughts in simple language instead of decorating the text.
source_quote: Если они есть, достаточно изложить их простым языком. Если мыслей нет, то колонке не помогут украшательства

instruction: Support claims with strong facts rather than impressive words.
source_quote: Но серьезность компании придают не красивые слова, а сильные факты.

instruction: Replace wordy everyday clichés with a single concrete word.
source_quote: Бытовые штампы безобидны во всем, кроме длины. Чаще всего эти многословные конструкции ужимаются до одного слова

instruction: Avoid corporate and advertising clichés that any company could use.
source_quote: Корпоративные и рекламные штампы - затертые фразы с сайтов, буклетов и наружной рекламы.

instruction: Tell the truth instead of hiding behind cowardly clichés.
source_quote: Идея в том, чтобы рассказать правду и не прятаться за трусливыми штампами

instruction: Lower the pompous tone to make your point more accessible and friendly.
source_quote: Журналист намеренно сбивает градус помпезности, чтобы сделать свою мысль более доступной.

instruction: Aim for a useful and respectful text, not a smart or respectable-sounding one.
source_quote: Но круто не надо. Респектабельно не надо. Надо полезно и уважительно.

instruction: Do not write phrases that could apply to anyone; make the text specific.
source_quote: Главная беда штампов в рекламе - кто угодно может их использовать. Если вы написали о себе со штампами, то точно такое же о себе может написать любая другая компания.

instruction: Не используйте корпоративные штампы вроде «молодая, динамично развивающаяся компания» — пишите о конкретной пользе для клиента.
source_quote: Лучше не писать о возрасте, если здесь не чем похвастаться. А даже если есть, возраст - не гарантия качества. Сосредоточьтесь на пользе для клиента

instruction: Вместо заявлений об опыте и профессионализме доказывайте их конкретными фактами.
source_quote: Докажите опыт и профессионализм: «Все инженеры прошли стажировку в компании «Бош» и знают о моторах всё».

instruction: Вместо «широкий спектр» перечисляйте товары как можно подробнее или описывайте ситуации их использования.
source_quote: Насколько возможно подробно перечислить товары, которые есть в наличии. Если их слишком много - напишите о ситуациях

instruction: Не пишите о расширении географии продаж — сообщайте только то, что нужно читателю: где вы сейчас продаете и куда доставляете.
source_quote: Ваш рост интересен только вам. Поэтому пишите только о том, что человеку нужно, где вы сейчас продаете и куда доставляете

instruction: Вместо «комплексный подход» и «под ключ» рассказывайте конкретно, что входит в работу и каков будет результат.
source_quote: Расскажите конкретно, что входит в «комплекс» и «под ключ», каков будет результат

instruction: Вместо обещаний «качественно и в срок» доказывайте, как именно вы обеспечите качество; если нечем — не пишите ничего.
source_quote: Докажите, что же такого хорошего вы сделаете. чтобы сдать работу качественно и в срок. Если ничего особенного – ничего не пишите.

instruction: Убирайте паразиты времени («в наши дни», «в современном мире», «сегодня») из начала предложений.
source_quote: Паразиты времени засоряют предложение бессмысленной информацией. Если их выбросить, время уточнить, а актуальность проблемы доказать, то предложение станет сильнее

instruction: Актуальность проблемы доказывайте фактами и источниками, а не указателями времени.
source_quote: По данным Water.org, 10 % населения Земли не имеет доступа к безопасной питьевой воде.

instruction: Используйте указатели времени только когда сравниваете настоящее с прошлым или будущим.
source_quote: Паразиты времени полезны, когда вы сравниваете настоящее с прошлым или будущим

instruction: Избавляйтесь от бюрократического языка везде, где можете.
source_quote: Избавляйтесь от бюрократского языка везде, где можете. Первый шаг - удаляйте паразиты времени, это проще всего.

instruction: Заменяйте канцеляризмы простыми формулировками.
source_quote: Канцеляризмы - штампы, которыми разговаривают бюрократы и руководители крупных постсоветских организаций

instruction: Никогда не прикрывайте канцеляризмами плохие новости — всегда выбирайте правду, даже неудобную.
source_quote: Всегда выбирайте правду, даже если она неудобная

instruction: Вместо назидательного тона используйте конкретные истории и примеры, в которых читатель узнает себя.
source_quote: Теперь проблема правдоподобна, а назидательности нет. Родители узнают в этой истории себя и захотят прочитать статью.

instruction: Replace bureaucratic stock phrases with one simple word.
source_quote: Учитесь видеть такие штампы и заменять на одно простое слово
